title: Silent Summit
subtitle: The cone that watches the islands

chapters.label: CHAPTER 01 · SUMMIT SILENCE
chapters.heading: A perfect cone against night sky.
chapters.body: Mount Fuji rises to 3,776.24 m, the highest point in Japan. Its symmetrical cone sits on Honshu about 100 km southwest of Tokyo and can be seen on clear days. The volcano last erupted between 1707 and 1708. Snow clings to its peak for five months each year.

heroImage.attribution: U.S. Navy photo by Lt. j.g. Andrew Leatherwood · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

chapters.label: CHAPTER 02 · CULTURAL SHADOW
chapters.heading: An ancient symbol of pilgrimage.
chapters.subheading: Artists have traced its outline for centuries.
chapters.body: Designated a Special Place of Scenic Beauty, Fuji belongs to Japan's Three Holy Mountains. The Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha shrine sits on its slopes. UNESCO listed it as a Cultural World Heritage Site in 2013, noting its influence on painters, poets and pilgrims across centuries.

heroImage.attribution: Romain Guy from San Francisco, USA · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

chapters.label: CHAPTER 03 · GEOTECTONIC HEART
chapters.heading: Three plates converge beneath its base.
chapters.body: The mountain rests on a triple junction where the Eurasian, North American and Philippine Sea plates meet. Subduction of the Pacific Plate drives its volcanic activity. Fuji lies near the Southwestern Japan Arc, the Northeastern Japan Arc and the Izu-Bonin-Mariana Arc, defining the region's geology.
